sample_unit: patients (federated training); 32,986 admissions in prospective evaluation

links.outcome: Effect of site-personalisation (local tuning) of the global model on performance
links.effect: Site-personalisation gave no significant overall improvement (AUROC improvement <0.01), which the authors read as high generalisability of the global model.
links.quote: Site-personalisation of the global model did not give a significant improvement in overall performance (AUROC improvement <0.01), suggesting high generalisability.

unlisted_practices: Federated learning across hospitals without patient data transfer
Low-cost edge hardware (Raspberry Pi) for privacy-preserving model development

screen.reason: The study empirically tests a federated learning deployment pipeline across four UK hospital trusts using microcomputing hardware, evaluating performance and generalisability gains compared to purely local training.

primary.practice: federated learning across multiple clinical sites
